description.short: A local full-stack web app that turns AI-sourced job leads into a focused pipeline for reviewing roles, managing applications, and tracking outreach.
long: I built this to keep each opportunity and its history together. Job postings, application files, and outreach stay connected as a role moves from review to application and follow-up.
Codex researches roles and contacts from inside the app. The interface shows its progress, failures, and requests for browser access, so the user can follow what it is doing.
I separated the agents that find jobs from the one that evaluates their fit. Their results must match an expected data structure before the app saves them to the database.

description.short: Tally Tracker is a cross-platform app for personal and shared counters on iOS, Android, and web, with real-time collaboration and offline synchronization.
long: A counter should respond as soon as you tap it. I made updates happen on the device first, with pending changes saved locally until they can reach the server.
Reconnecting can send the same update more than once. The server recognizes repeated requests so a retry does not count the same change twice, while live updates keep shared counters in sync.
I also had to account for how sign-in differs across platforms. Browser sessions use cookies; mobile sessions use secure device storage. Both can refresh an expired session before retrying a request.

description.short: A reaction-time training app with timed drills, animated feedback, user accounts, and performance history, backed by a secure Express/PostgreSQL API.
long: I used GSAP to coordinate the countdown, target feedback, and results screen while keeping animation separate from the game rules. The same approach carries into the profile, where filters and history columns move into place as the view changes.
A score is more useful when you know how it was earned. I built the API to save the drill settings with each result, so players can revisit an attempt and compare results from similar drills.

description.short: A real-time tic-tac-toe lobby with JWT-authenticated Socket.IO sessions, server-side move validation, rematches, forfeits, and disconnect recovery.
long: I built the client and server around one shared version of each match. The server checks whose turn it is and whether a move is valid before sending the updated board to both players.
A brief connection loss gives the player 30 seconds to return before forfeiting. I also track connections per user so opening another tab does not replace the existing session.
The tests play matches through actual socket connections. They cover the path from joining a game to wins, draws, and rematches through the same handlers that run live play.
